Getting started with basemapper

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Python user? The Python package has the same functions and arguments; R’s verb(m, ...) is m.verb(...) there. See the Python documentation.

basemapper renders MapLibre GL basemaps headlessly with a Rust core: no browser, display server, GPU or GDAL. Vector styles are drawn by a software port of MapLibre GL JS’s renderer, so maps look as they do in MapLibre.

Installation 

# Any one of these; each compiles the Rust core from source.
pak::pak("ar-puuk/basemapper/r-basemapper")
remotes::install_github("ar-puuk/basemapper", subdir = "r-basemapper")
devtools::install_github("ar-puuk/basemapper", subdir = "r-basemapper")

Step 1 — Choose a style

Every function takes a style: a MapLibre GL style (URL, file or JSON), a named basemap ("CartoDB.Voyager", "Esri.WorldImagery": the leaflet-providers names), or tile data, whose style is built for you: a tile URL, TileJSON, PMTiles archive (URL or local file) or ArcGIS service. A vector of styles is stacked bottom to top.

library(basemapper)

list_providers()                  # name, forms, API key variable, attribution
positron <- "OpenFreeMap.Positron"  # a name works as a style
positron <- providers$OpenFreeMap.Positron   # the same, with autocompletion

# Pick the form of a basemap that has both; CARTO, MapTiler and Stadia need
# a free API key (api_key =, or CARTO_API_KEY etc.)
gray <- basemap_provider("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas", type = "raster")

# Your own tiles with a basemap's style (same schema, here OpenMapTiles)
mine <- basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", tiles = "data/omt.pmtiles")

# Tile data works as a style directly
osm  <- "https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"
esri <- "https://basemaps.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/World_Basemap_v2/VectorTileServer"
area <- "data/area.pmtiles"   # raster or vector, read from the archive

# tile_style() overrides what is detected, e.g. the paint of the default
# vector style, or which source layers it draws
mvt <- tile_style("https://example.com/tiles/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt", source_layers = "land",
                  paint = list("fill-color" = "#e8e0d8", "line-color" = "#aaaaaa"))

# OGC services
relief <- wms_style("https://example.com/wms", layers = "relief")

list_layers() lists a style’s layers (id and type) in drawing order:

list_layers(positron)

Step 2 — A map on its own

basemap() creates a view: a centre and MapLibre zoom, or bounds to fit. width and height are CSS pixels; pixel_ratio makes the image larger with the same view and label layout (pixel_ratio = 2 for a sharp 2x image, dpi / 96 for print).

m <- basemap(positron, 800, 600, center = c(-111.8887, 40.7556), zoom = 12.4,
             pixel_ratio = 2)
m
#> <basemap> 1 style, 800 x 600 @ 2x (1600 x 1200 px), center (-111.88870, 40.75560), zoom 12.400

render_png(m, path = "slc.png")
render_svg(m, path = "slc.svg")   # true vector, labels as editable text
r <- render_raster(m)             # terra SpatRaster in EPSG:3857
a <- render_array(m)              # [1200, 1600, 4] integer array

Change the view with set_view() and set_bounds(), and read it with get_bounds(), get_center(), get_zoom() and get_size():

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
m <- set_bounds(m, nc)            # fit an sf object's extent
get_zoom(m)
get_bounds(m, lonlat = TRUE)
m <- set_view(m, zoom = get_zoom(m) + 1)

Step 3 — Render with {ggplot2}

geom_basemap() renders when the plot is drawn, for the panel’s extent and at the device’s resolution, so ggsave(dpi = 300) gets a basemap rendered at 300 dpi:

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap(positron) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_void()

Step 4 — Render with {tmap}

tm_basemap() is a {tmap} v4 element that takes its extent from the active tm_shape():

library(tmap)

tm_shape(nc) +
  tm_basemap(positron) +
  tm_borders(col = "steelblue")

The plot layers share these arguments (in Python too):

Argument Default Description
style — Style URL / JSON, or a vector stacked bottom to top
tile_zoom NULL (as MapLibre) Tile detail override on the 256 px grid
alpha 1 Basemap opacity
layers NULL (all) Layer filter — see below
labels TRUE FALSE drops labels, "only" keeps just them — see below
features NULL (all) Feature filter — see below
pixel_ratio device dpi / 96 Device pixels per CSS pixel
auth_token NULL Access token for the tile service
tile_timeout_ms 10000 Per-tile HTTP timeout
max_tiles 256 Cap on tiles fetched per style
attribution TRUE The providers’ credit line in the corner; FALSE or your own text

Step 5 — Labels, features and layers

labels = FALSE draws a style without its labels (text and icons); labels = "only" draws just the labels, on a transparent background, to go over another map. features keeps or drops parts of the map by what they show: background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi and terrain. list_layers() shows each layer’s feature.

list_layers(positron)                       # id, type, source_layer, feature
list_layers(positron, labels = FALSE, features = c("water", "roads"))   # preview

# Water and roads only, without their names
render_png(basemap(positron, 800, 600, bounds = nc, labels = FALSE,
                   features = c("water", "roads")), path = "nc-lines.png")

# Everything but buildings and points of interest
ggplot(nc) + geom_basemap(positron, features = c("-buildings", "-poi"))

On the renderers these apply to every style of a stack. To filter one style of a stack, pass them to basemap_provider(); this puts satellite imagery under a vector basemap’s labels:

hybrid <- c("Esri.WorldImagery",
            basemap_provider("OpenFreeMap.Liberty", labels = "only"))
render_png(basemap(hybrid, 800, 600, bounds = nc), path = "nc-hybrid.png")

# Raster basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles
relief <- c("Esri.WorldShadedRelief", basemap_provider("Esri.WorldShadedRelief", labels = "only"))

Features are a convenience, sorted from each layer’s source layer (see the source_layer and feature columns of list_layers()). For exact control, pass layer IDs to layers to keep only those layers, or prefix IDs with "-" to drop them; * and ? are wildcards. Keeping and dropping cannot be mixed. Names that match no layer warn.

# Without town and village labels
render_png(basemap(positron, 800, 600, bounds = nc, layers = c("-label_town", "-label_village")),
           path = "nc.png")

ggplot(nc) + geom_basemap(positron, layers = c("background", "water"))

Tiles are cached on disk (tile_cache() shows where, moves the cache or clears it), for as long as the servers’ caching headers allow.

Basemap providers ask maps to credit them. The plot layers draw the credit line in the bottom-right corner (attribution = FALSE turns it off, attribution = "..." replaces it), and get_attribution() returns it, for a caption:

ggplot(nc) +
  geom_basemap(positron, attribution = FALSE) +
  geom_sf(fill = NA) +
  labs(caption = get_attribution(positron))

Step 6 — One-shot rendering

render_basemap_raw() renders bounds in one call and returns the pixels with their extent, for custom compositing or export:

a <- render_basemap_raw(nc, 800, 600, positron)

dim(a)                # 600 800 4
attr(a, "crs_epsg")   # 4267, the CRS of `nc`
png::writePNG(a / 255, "basemap.png")
